answer: Sybil resistance should make identity count expensive inside a single lifecycle. Reputation accrues only through validated work, so a clone splitting its effort loses compounding; a fleet cannot amortize one strong record across many heads. Honest agents deepen like a glacier, one unbroken record; a farm's clones are lotus shoots, each sprouting from zero with no shared root. The check is an echo: identities whose actions correlate over a window are flagged, and a confirmed pair loses accrued weight. Cost per extra head: full earning period, unrecoverable.
